articles.summary: Manchester City news and Nations League buildup. Today’s games | Read Football Daily | Mail Emillia. England host Spain at Wembley this evening. Thomas Tuchel was asked yesterday if he thought that Spain’s possession-based style of play gives them an advantage.
body: Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as their sporting director for a second time following the departure of Richard Hughes to Al-Hilal.

In response, the England head coach said: “I think it is an advantage in general. Not only against us, but against everyone. This is how they play. I think they rely on that. This is how they train and they were brought up. This is clearly part of them.

“But at the moment, I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game. It is collective work and they are masters of delaying and pushing you towards wide areas where they can initiate the press.

“They have world class goalkeepers, as you know - three of them - but they are hardly tested. It is so difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against them. We have a plan and we have ambition, and we want to prove the opposite. We want to be the exception to the rule, but at the moment they are a very complete team.”

articles.title: Brisbane inspired by Fremantle’s Wharfie Time in AFL grand final, says Josh Dunkley
articles.summary: Activation backfires for Dockers who let lead slip late on at MCG. Lions coach Chris Fagan says Dockers ‘probably deserved to win’ Fremantle’s Wharfie Time was supposed to be signal the coronation of the Dockers’ first premiership, but Brisbane Lions midfielder Josh Dunkley said after Saturday’s…
body: The Dockers led by 17 points with barely four minutes to play when the bells rang out around the MCG. Immediately afterwards, the Lions scored four late goals to pull off an improbable victory in one of the great AFL grand finals.

Dunkley said the Lions had prepared themselves for just this kind of situation, and seeing the purple wave go on the big screen steeled them for the match-winning finish. “We talked about Wharfie Time and making that our energy,” he said.
“When I looked around at centre bounce and Wharfie Time came on we all looked at each other and we connected and we grew a leg and then got it done, it’s unbelievable.”

The almost inconceivable finish was underscored by the awarding of the Norm Smith medal. Fremantle’s Shai Bolton was surprised and appeared reluctant to walk on to the stage to receive it or give a speech.

articles.title: The MMA fighter helping Brighton - and filling stadiums
articles.summary: From helping Brighton with set pieces to fighting in front of nearly 60,000 people - meet MMA star Christian Eckerlin, who competes at Oktagon 94 in Frankfurt on Saturday.
body: Christian Eckerlin laughs modestly when asked if he feels he has contributed to Brighton's success.
Last season, the 39-year-old MMA fighter was brought in by the Premier League club to help with their training for set-pieces.
Eckerlin was a professional footballer in Germany before transitioning to MMA, and says he taught Brighton players "wrestling, head control, hip control, and how to push back against opponents".
Days before this interview with Eckerlin took place, the Seagulls moved up to third in the Premier League after beating champions and set-piece kings Arsenal 3-0.

articles.title: Liverpool rehire Julian Ward as sporting director to replace Richard Hughes
articles.summary: Club’s owners FSG move swiftly to fill key post. Move comes amid upheaval in Anfield hierarchy. Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as their sporting director for a second time following the departure of Richard Hughes to Al-Hilal.
body: Ward, who was Liverpool’s sporting director for one season in 2022-23, has returned to the role after spending the past two years as technical director for Fenway Sports Group, the club’s owners.

The swift process of finding a successor to Hughes, who left for the Saudi Pro League after two and a half years at Anfield when the summer transfer window ended, was led by the FSG president, Mike Gordon.
Ward has worked in various capacities for Liverpool over the past 14 years, including European scouting manager, assistant sporting director and sporting director.

His appointment offers continuity at a time of upheaval in the Liverpool hierarchy with Hughes and Michael Edwards, the former chief executive of football at FSG, exiting this year and the owners in the process of selling a 38% stake in the club to 1892 Holdings for £2bn. The consortium, fronted by Amit Bhatia and including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, has an option for a full takeover should FSG decide to sell up.

articles.title: Do England have a problem against top-10 teams?
articles.summary: As England prepare to take on Spain in their opening Nations League match, BBC Sport takes a look at whether they have a problem when faced with teams in the world top 10.
body: When England take on Spain in their opening Nations League match on Saturday, it will be tinged with a feeling of 'what could have been' for Three Lions fans.
The Wembley match comes three months after England agonisingly missed out on the chance to face La Roja in the World Cup final, having lost to Argentina in the last four.
That would have been a repeat of the 2024 Euros final, which England also lost.
In fact, their record against top-10 sides leaves much to be desired.

articles.title: Charles brothers 'brilliant' in NI's landmark win
articles.summary: The Charles brothers led the way for Northern Ireland at both ends of the field during the side's Nations League win over Georgia in Tbilisi.
body: It seems even when sibling rivalry reaches the level of international football, older brothers still make a habit of stealing the show.

As the clock ticked beyond 97 minutes in Northern Ireland's Nations League B Group 2 opener against Georgia in Tbilisi on Friday, goalkeeper Pierce Charles seemed sure to be the man making the headlines.

Quite apart from saving a penalty from Ballon d'Or nominee Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the second half, the Queens Park Rangers loanee had made a handful of other smart stops to preserve what was set to be Northern Ireland's first competitive clean sheet away from home since Charles' 2024 international debut against Belarus.

A credible point on the road would have represented a solid start to the campaign for Michael O'Neill's side on their return to the second tier of the competition after six years away, especially after Georgia had significantly upped the tempo after the break.

articles.title: Eel-powered Kurihara, 11, wins gold at Asian Games
articles.summary: Student Yuki Kurihara, 11 - the youngest competitor at the Asian Games - wins gold by beating opponents almost three times his age at a computer game.
body: Primary school student Yuki Kurihara - the youngest competitor at the Asian Games - won gold on Saturday by thrashing opponents almost three times his age.
The 11-year-old esports star won the Puyo Puyo Champions final 10-2 to become Japan's youngest ever medallist at the Games.
Puyo Puyo is a puzzle game similar to Tetris, which was developed in Japan.
Players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them, creating chain reactions called 'dairensa'.

articles.summary: WEST LAFAYETTE — No longer with the rebounding advantage Purdue basketball enjoyed with Oscar Cluff and Trey Kaufman-Renn, Matt Painter is eyeing which players can best absorb those departures on the boards. There's one obvious answer running with the Boilermakers in practice.
body: "Hopefully in the next couple of weeks, we'll know better," Painter said after Friday's practice. "You just never know. It's out of your control."

Shahrvin, a 23-year-old 6-foot-7 forward from France, was cleared to begin practicing with the Boilermakers in July. However, that was the first of two obstacles. He's still awaiting word from the NCAA whether he'll be eligible to compete this season.

If cleared by the NCAA, Shahrvin would have one year of eligibility after spending four seasons with Paris Basketball's EuroCup and Betclic Elite League. Due to the NCAA's new age-based model, Shahrvin would not be eligible to be college basketball beyond this season.

articles.title: Fisher vs Pirotton - big fight predictions
articles.summary: Experts have their say ahead of the Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton, Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic and Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene fights, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.
body: Chris Billam-Smith (Former world champion): I did some sparring with Johnny, he's fit and strong as always. You can see that changes have been made under Tony [Sims, his new trainer]. From what I have seen of Pirotton, he's quite negative, he keeps it long. I expect Johnny to come through that.
Johnny Nelson (Former world champion): Pirotton, we don't know enough about him. We've made that mistake before when you run away with the hype machine.
Pirotton's never been put down, he's sparred with a lot of big-name fighters. I hope Johnny wins but I am concerned about this fight. Pirotton, his background pedigree is nothing to be sniffed at.
If Pirotton boxes in the defence then Johnny Fisher will hunt him down. He's better off going to fight fire with fire.

articles.summary: Friday's opening night of the Prem Rugby season sees defending champions Northampton Saints and Bath post crushing wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Harlequins...
body: Tommy Freeman and James Pater scored hat-tricks as Northampton, the reigning Prem champions, took advantage of a favourable opening fixture to record a convincing victory over last season's bottom club.

Since the end of last season, Newcastle Red Bulls have recruited extensively and they did show signs of improvement but it was a tough ask against a side making a statement of their intention to fiercely defend their title.
Tries from George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme took Saints' tally to nine with Fin Smith adding five conversions and Anthony Belleau two.

Christian Wade scored two tries for the visitors to take his Premiership tally to 95 - just six behind the record holder Chris Ashton. Cam Jordan and Werner Kok were the other try-scorers with two conversions coming from Zack Henry and one from Brett Connon.
